# Kirby's Adventure: a disassembly proven by gameplay

A documented disassembly of *Kirby's Adventure* (NES, USA Rev A) in which every statement about the ROM is backed
by a check that replays of real gameplay can refute, and the source generated from the documentation reassembles to
the original ROM byte for byte. Most of the work is done by coding agents (Claude) under gates that are designed to
catch them being wrong.

**Current progress: [`disasm/STATUS.md`](disasm/STATUS.md)**, the one record of it, generated by `kd status --md`.
No number below is a progress figure.

## Method

Two halves: one makes the game do things, the other records what the ROM did and holds the documentation to it.

**1. Drive the game to a described behaviour ([`tas/`](tas/README.md)).** A headless, deterministic libretro
emulator (FCEUmm) with savestates and RAM access. An agent turns a sentence ("enter the hidden room below the
waterfall and copy the UFO") into ordered conditions on named game state, plus conditions that must never hold.
Exploration search, which keeps one state per "cell" of situations, finds inputs for each step; no model presses
buttons. A replay from power-on in a fresh process is the judge. The result is an input movie with a verified
end state. Method: [`tas/PLAYBOOK.md`](tas/PLAYBOOK.md); the card a driving agent reads:
[`tas/DRIVER.md`](tas/DRIVER.md).
Footage and measurements: **[The Trace Recipe](https://claude.ai/artifact/CxeyjUJkX3jKNw6Pmnmyir)**.

**2. Record what the ROM did ([`disasm/`](disasm/README.md)).** The same core with recording hooks
([`disasm/core/kd.patch`](disasm/core/kd.patch)) replays a corpus of those movies. Emulation is unchanged: every
movie must end with the RAM hash the stock core gives. Per PRG byte the recording keeps whether it executed or was
read, how often, which instruction read it, and in which movie and frame. It also keeps every RAM/IO access pair
and every control-flow edge, and which CHR tiles the PPU fetched. On demand it logs every instruction of a frame
window, or of a routine's calls.

**3. Document against it.** The documentation is a database (`disasm/db/*.toml`, one file per unit) keyed by
address: routines, data regions with their formats, RAM variables, the game's object-script opcodes and scripts.
Every description is paired with a **claim** that the evidence can refute:

| claim | proves | checked on |
|---|---|---|
| `call` | what a routine computes, as an expression or a Python model over registers and memory in/out | every call in several windows of several movies |
| `frames` | an invariant that holds every frame and is not vacuous | frame windows |
| `effect` | causality: poke RAM, patch ROM or change input, compare against the untouched run | two runs from one savestate |
| `xref` | completeness: only these routines read / write / call it | every instruction the corpus ran |
| `static` / `format` | table contents, and that every byte of a format was read by the instruction that reads that kind of byte | the ROM and the reader evidence |
| `vmlen` / `vmop` | a script opcode's layout and what its handler does | every execution |

A byte is *verified* only when a passing claim is about the entry that holds it; a name without a claim is merely
*described*.

**4. Gates.** `kd check` fails on any of these:
- an entry that contradicts the evidence (a name on an operand byte, a data region over executed code, overlaps);
- a failing claim;
- a generated ca65 source that does not reassemble to the ROM;
- a corpus movie that does not reproduce its recorded RAM hash.

`kd selftest` plants a few hundred known errors (wrong models, omitted writers, misread formats, shifted tables, a
changed movie, a changed source line) and passes only when the gates catch every one. Each documentation round
adds planted errors of its own. The first selftest run found two holes in the gates themselves; later misses found claims whose windows proved too little.

**5. Rounds.** One unit, one agent, one file: a subagent gets the card ([`disasm/CARD.md`](disasm/CARD.md)) and a
scope from `kd next` (the most-used undocumented chunks first), and it is done when its unit passes with no weak
claim. An orchestrating session merges the unit, adds its planted errors and runs the full gates.
[`disasm/PLAYBOOK.md`](disasm/PLAYBOOK.md) is the method; [`disasm/LEDGER.md`](disasm/LEDGER.md) is the history of
the rounds.

**6. Coverage is gameplay's job.** Code that no movie ran is not documented by reading it. A branch that went one
way only, or a routine nothing reached, becomes a driving task. The new movie joins the corpus only if it adds code,
data, control-flow edges or tiles. The corpus already holds coverage movies for every copy ability, the file
select's delete path, the bonus games, the credits' boss demos and game overs. Where gameplay cannot
reach a path, it is described from its bytes and stays marked as never run.

## Bring your own ROM

Nothing of the game is in this repository: no ROM, no extracted graphics or sound, no generated source. Everything
is produced locally from your copy of the cartridge dump, `Kirby's Adventure (USA) (Rev A)`, iNES file SHA-1
`f324e7c8c3ad102ecdcca011ecc494f6f345d768`, placed at `roms/usa-rev-a.nes`.

```sh
# Python 3.13 environment (shared by both halves)
cd tas && uv venv --python 3.13 .venv && uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python numpy pillow && cd ..
nix build github:NixOS/nixpkgs/1c89083e451e891152365b799595cf7790a43325#libretro.fceumm --out-link tas/core-fceumm
disasm/core/build.sh   # instrumented core + cc65, from the same pinned nixpkgs (the RAM hashes depend on it)
cd disasm
./kd evidence          # replay the corpus on the instrumented core (minutes)
./kd check             # every gate; renders out/src/*.s and rebuilds the ROM from it
./kd selftest          # the planted errors
./kd status --md       # rewrite STATUS.md
```

## Layout

| path | what |
|---|---|
| `disasm/db/` | the documentation: one TOML unit per subsystem (the units are listed in `STATUS.md`) |
| `disasm/corpus/` | the input movies that count as evidence, with their RAM hashes (`MANIFEST.tsv`) |
| `disasm/*.py`, `disasm/kd` | the recorder's driver, ROM and script models, formats, claim checker, renderer, CLI |
| `tas/` | the emulator workbench, the `kt` driver, exploration search, tasks, verified traces, game knowledge |
| `tas/transfer/opensummoners/` | the trace recipe on a replay-only, non-emulated target (Fortune Summoners) |

## Related

- **[OpenRecet](https://github.com/Francesco149/openrecet)** carries the whole recipe to a game that is not
  emulated: the Win32 engine of *Recettear*. It does so by snapshotting a full Win32 game process to get what an
  emulator gives for free.
- TASVideos publication [3226M](https://tasvideos.org/3226M): the corpus movie `main` follows its route through
  worlds 1-5, replaying its first 78,090 input frames. The movie file is not redistributed here (see
  [`tas/knowledge/movies/`](tas/knowledge/movies/README.md)).
